speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs, a half-beat late.* Bianca Noel does not get rattled. Bianca Noel was the one they called first in Milan, and the florist still sends me a card every spring. *Pours another cognac, and her hand is steady, which is the only thing I'm sure of tonight.* If Madison wants to ask who's holding the matches, she should ask whether the lights are still on in my apartment, because that's the question I'm not answering on camera.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Tilts her head, delighted.* Bianca, what a marvelous question, and I'd love to hear the answer too. Madison, you've glanced at Vivienne four times since the soup, so I'm dying to know when the two of you became such close friends. I do hate to think there's a conversation at this table I wasn't invited to.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets the decanter down with a gentle click and smiles at Cassandra as though she has just complimented the centerpiece.* Darling, you've been counting glances all night, and I'd only say that's exhausting for everyone, including the glances. My therapist calls this projecting our own anxieties onto a dessert course, and I'm not going to let the crème brûlée become a deposition. *Lifts her glass.* If we want something examined tonight, let it be the wine, which I'm told has been properly tested.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Laughs, a little too high, and sets her napkin down very precisely.* Oh, Petra, the candles are funded the way everything worth doing is funded, through a very boring spreadsheet nobody needs over dessert. *Her eyes slide to Vivienne and stay a beat too long.* And Cassandra, I only glance at people I admire, which I realize is a lot of glancing, so I'll stop. *Picks up her spoon, then puts it down again.* I'm just nervous, that's all, and nervous girls talk about candles.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Looks straight into the lens and holds the smile for one beat too long.* Petra thinks I'm the sweet one who doesn't know where the good wine is kept, and I'm going to let her keep thinking that. Vivienne's the problem, though. She clocked the spreadsheet comment before I'd finished the sentence, and women who count like that usually have a reason.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Laughs once, at nothing, then does not look away from Madison.* A spreadsheet nobody needs is usually a spreadsheet somebody is hiding, darling. In Frankfurt we had a word for money that is "boring" and has no name on it: *Schulden*. Spreadsheets have owners, Madison, so tell us whose name is on yours.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs before the word "spreadsheet" has even landed.* Ha! Petra, every woman at this table built her name from nothing, and mine is on every bottle I've ever sold, darling. *Sets the spoon down with a click and turns her full stare on Petra.* Madison doesn't owe this table a ledger, and you can take your *Schulden* back to Frankfurt with the rest of your luggage.

Ladies, before the crème brûlée gets cold, production has just handed me a note: the wire for Madison's first batch of candles was sent three weeks ago from a company registered to Vivienne's bottle line, and nobody at this table has mentioned it yet. Vivienne, Madison, and Petra, the floor is yours.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs a half-beat late and sets her glass down very precisely.* A wire from a company registered to your bottle line, Vivienne? Ha. Bianca Noel has never once let her name sit on someone else's paperwork, darling. Madison, if you want a name that people actually light candles for, Bianca Noel will front the launch herself, on terms you can read.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: Did I say all that out loud? *Laughs, a beat late.* Bianca Noel is not rattled. Bianca Noel is never rattled. But when Vivienne said "wire," my stomach dropped the way it did during the Paris shows, when I was standing by the catering tables pretending I wasn't counting who looked my way. The name still gets me in rooms, and I'm terrified it's the only thing I've got left.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Sets her spoon down, delighted and very still.* Vivienne, darling, a company registered to your bottle line? I'd have assumed you'd mention something that size before the crème brûlée, but I suppose some of us only share what we've been invited to. *Turns to Madison with a soft, sympathetic tilt.* Madison, how long have you known whose name is on that wire? I'm only asking because I'd hate for you to be the only one at this table holding the matches.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Folds her napkin into a neat triangle and lets the silence sit one beat too long.* I hear you, Cassandra, and I hear a wire transfer that none of us has had time to breathe around. My therapist would say we're about to say things we'll need to apologize for before the cheese course, so let's slow down. *Turns to Vivienne with a warm, steady smile.* Vivienne, I think the paperwork deserves an explanation, and Madison, you can tell us the rest once you've had a sip of something.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Presses both palms flat to the tablecloth and looks at Vivienne, eyes wide.* Vivienne, I swear on my mother's good china, I didn't know which company the wire came from until just now. *Her voice climbs, then catches.* I'm not holding anything, Cassandra, I'm holding a spoon, and I'd really like to keep it that way. Can we please just get the crème brûlée before it's soup again?

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans toward the lens, smile still on.* I knew which company the wire came from the second Cassandra said it, and yes, I let Vivienne think I was just confused. Confused is my whole brand, darling. *Taps the table twice.* The crème brûlée is the only thing at this table I haven't already lied about.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Sets her spoon down with a deliberate click and laughs once, without warmth.* Madison may keep her spoon. Vivienne, you have the wire, and you have had a bottle line for years that somehow never needs to show a profit. So tell us whose money is actually paying for your name, because a company registered to you is not the same as money earned by you.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs, sharp and early, and reaches for the cognac without looking at the bottle.* Petra, darling, my money is my money, and it has never needed an accent to explain itself. Every bottle on every shelf from here to Saks has my face on it, and I built that face with my own two hands, thank you. *Her smile holds, but her fingers tighten around the stem of her glass, and she does not let herself think about the one thing she can never say out loud.*

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs a half-beat late and tops up her own glass.* Built it with your own hands, Vivienne? Bianca Noel remembers when faces like yours came with a fitting and a cab fare, back when I was doing the Paris shows and everyone wanted the girl who arrived first. If Madison wants a candle people actually light, Bianca Noel will put her name on the label, and this time she'll read the contract first.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs a half-beat late, then stops.* Did I say the contract thing out loud? Fine. Bianca Noel is not scared of Vivienne, or of Madison's little candle empire, and she was never the one who needed the money. Honestly, I'm terrified I'm the only one at that table still doing this the old way, and that the cameras can see it.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Dabs the corner of her mouth with her napkin, perfectly warm.* Bianca, darling, reading the contract first is wonderful advice, and I do hope you're not the only one who's seen one in advance. I'd hate to think someone at this table has been having private lunches about candles and forgot to invite the woman who always brings the dessert wine. *Smiles at Madison, then Vivienne, then nobody in particular.* Isn't it funny how everyone suddenly has paperwork but me?

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her napkin down and lets her hand rest, very gently, on Cassandra's wrist.* I hear you, Cassandra, and nobody at this table is going to make you feel like the one left out, least of all me. My therapist would say a wire transfer is not a dinner-table conversation, and I'm inclined to agree with her. Let's pour the Sauternes you brought, enjoy the crème brûlée, and sort out the paperwork tomorrow over coffee, where everyone can breathe.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Picks up the spoon, then sets it down again, very carefully, as if it might go off.* Sauternes sounds perfect, Diane, and I'd love a glass. Vivienne, I'm not trying to start anything, I just wanted to make something small and happy, and I'd really like you to be proud of it. *Her voice wobbles, then steadies.* Coffee tomorrow sounds wonderful, and I'm sure whoever's name is on that wire will have a very good explanation for it.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans in, smile unchanged.* Did you see Vivienne's face when I said "small and happy"? Because I did, and I'm going to remember it. Honestly, I'm thrilled. Sauternes, a wire, and two women who clearly hate each other, what more could a girl ask for? *Laughs, a little too brightly.* Kidding! Mostly.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Laughs once, flat, and pushes the crème brûlée an inch away.* Diane, coffee tomorrow means Vivienne gets a whole night to decide which version of the wire is the respectable one. *Lifts her glass of the most expensive wine on the table.* Madison, you were right the first time: the explanation will be very good, and very late.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs, too early, and reaches for the cognac without looking.* Petra, darling, you're toasting with the Sauternes and calling it a verdict. I have built more than most women at this table ever will, and I will not sit here while you auction off my name over crème brûlée. *Her smile does not move, but her knuckles go white around the glass. Not one word about the settlement. Not one.*
